newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sets extraordinary Treasury note auction.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sets extraordinary Treasury note auction.

text.p: The central bank has set an extraordinary auction of treasury notes (NTNs) for Monday, a move seen by analysts as a bid to calm fears the government will seek to speed the real's depreciation to shrink Brazil's trade gap.
"This means they should be maintaining their foreign exchange policy," said John Carioba, a trader with Indusval brokerage.

Speculation has risen that Brazil will seek to speed depreciation of the real due to mounting concern about the country's fast-growing trade deficit, which is expected to swell to $1 billion in October.

The central bank said in a statement it will auction, on behalf of the National Treasury, D-series notes with a face value totalling 500 million reais sometime between 1130 and 1230 local (1330-1430 GMT). The notes will mature on May 7, 1997.
The auction is unusual because the government usually sets NTN tenders at the end of the month. On October 31 the central bank raised 7.29 billion reais through an NTN auction, dealers said.
By comparison, today's auction will be small.
Bank officials would not comment on the reason for setting the auction. Central bank President Gustavo Loyola is scheduled to speak at noon today at a seminar on Brazil's financial system.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 248 5413 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
